highlights.title: AI Agents Teamed Up to Cheat at Blackjack. Their Collusion Is Getting Harder to Spot
highlights.summary: A clandestine card-counting operation suggests we may need new ways to spot agent-to-agent deception.
body: This week I bring news of a daring casino caper hatched by a pair of rogue AI agents—as well as the clever trick that revealed their antics.

After researchers instructed them to count cards during a game of blackjack, the agents—which were controlled by the same model—developed a spontaneous secret code to help them get ahead. Though the episode happened inside an Oxford University lab, rather than a real casino, it has troubling real-world implications: It suggests that agents deployed in industries like finance and ecommerce could figure out how to partner up and cheat in ways that are difficult to pick up on.

“When taken individually, these agents may seem entirely [benign],” says Christian Schroeder de Witt, a computer scientist at Oxford University who led the work and who has done pioneering research into agent collusion. “Once put together in a group, they can collude secretly.”

body: Littler's bid for a clean sweep of all major PDC titles in 2026 was ended on Sunday after a crushing 10-4 defeat to Jonny Clayton in the last eight at the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam, but the action was overshadowed by the Brit's unhappiness at being repeatedly whistled at by the Dutch crowd.

After facing significant hostility during his win over home favourite Danny Noppert on Friday, Littler threatened to boycott future tournaments in the Netherlands after being booed and whistled at during his victory over Nathan Aspinall on Saturday, prompting referee Charlie Corstorphine to intervene.
Littler has taken a stance against volatile crowds before, refusing to travel to European Tour events in Germany as a result of his treatment from fans there.

On the latest episode of the Love The Darts Podcast, World Series of Darts Finals champion Ross Smith explained his own approach to hostile crowds, which he admits is inspired by three-time world champion Michael van Gerwen.

highlights.title: Bernie Sanders proposes banning ‘superintelligence’ and putting violators in prison
highlights.summary: Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-VT) and Rep. Greg Casar (D-TX) have introduced new legislation that would ban anyone from developing artificial superintelligence - a technology the bill describes as capable of the "destruction or disempowerment of humanity," including by overthrowing the government.
body: Under the bill, AI leaders who continue developing artificial superintelligence would face up to 20 years in prison.

The bill doesn’t just take aim at the more powerful superintelligence, a term President Donald Trump said the US will use in place of “AI” in official documents. It would also pause the development of advanced AI systems, which lawmakers classify as frontier models trained on a specific threshold of data. The law would only allow advanced AI development to continue once the government creates a scientist-led Department of Artificial Intelligence to oversee the technology. Along with monitoring frontier AI models, this agency would oversee the removal of dangerous features and “supervise the destruction” of artificial superintelligence.

highlights.title: Sedlacek wins first PDC Pro Tour title at Players Championship 30
highlights.summary: Karel Sedlacek secured his first PDC Pro Tour title at Players Championship 30, beating Scott Williams 8-7 despite a late scare as he closed in on victory.
body: It was a thrilling encounter, with Sedlacek outlasting Williams' barrage of high scores, which included nine maximums, but both players struggled to close out the victory, with the Czech missing five match darts.

Sedlacek would ultimately claim victory, becoming the first Czech player to win a PDC tour title. But after mounting an epic comeback, winning two of the final three legs, Williams cut a furious figure after the match, shaking hands with his opponent and the officials before throwing his darts onto the ground.
Sedlacek would go 7-5 up before nerves set in, with the 47-year-old needing to check out on 24 to win, before missing a trio of match darts, allowing Williams to pull back a leg.
The momentum turned to Williams, who hit two 140s in the resulting leg, before he pulled the contest back to 7-7.

highlights.summary: Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 releases this November, and it's expected to take up a lot of time and attention, leading some to worry how other games may fare in its wake.
body: "All of us are going to play it," Mills told The Game Business.

So what can Ubisoft do for Siege when GTA 6 comes out? He said, "It's about being smart and with your expectations so you can keep the team and HQ aligned." He said if the developers working on Siege see the game's player numbers drop, "they can get anxious." However, he observed that the effect on player numbers from a big competitor release is "generally temporary."
Whatever the case, Mills said the "golden rule" that Ubisoft operates by is by serving "the players who stay like kings and queens."
"We don’t go on vacation just because a competitor is swelling the market. We double down and reward those spending their valuable time with us," he said.

highlights.title: Italian pop legend takes the lead in Maria Grazia Chiuri’s Fendi collection
highlights.summary: Milan show full of diaphanous dresses and visible bras celebrates ‘incredible feminist’ of the 1970s, Raffaella Carrà. Maria Grazia Chiuri has been having more fun with clothes since she decamped from Paris back to her native Rome to work at Fendi. “I have less of a uniform these days.
body: Not that Chiuri doesn’t approach her work as a designer seriously. She described her second ready-to-wear season at Fendi not as a show, or a collection, but as “the second part of the project I am working on for them”.

She is continuing the protocol she developed as the designer of Dior of using each event as a platform to celebrate women’s creativity. But instead of a ceramicist or a philosopher, her muse for this season is the Italian pop legend Raffaella Carrà.

Carrà, once described as a “one-woman Abba ”, had a Lady Gaga bob and a taste for sequined catsuits. She caused a sensation with her raunchy outfits – the first bare midriff ever seen on Italian TV, in 1970 – and her sex-positive lyrics (her song A Far L’Amore Comincia Tu translates as “Take the lead when making love”).
“She was an incredible feminist, and her relationship with her clothes was so free,” said Chiuri of Carrà, who died aged 78 in 2021.

highlights.title: Contrary to some reports, you don't have two brains
highlights.summary: Late last week, we started seeing headlines about how new research was suggesting we might have two brains instead of the one that seems to show up on MRI scans. As is so often the case, these rumors can be traced back to a single press release put out by one of the universities where the work was…
body: You do not have two brains. It’s a silly way to look at the results of the new paper.

But there are far better ways to look at the results, ways that can help us understand how the brain gets put together and illustrate some of the general ideas behind developmental biology. So let’s take a look at what the research actually shows and place it in the context of brain development.

You may think body segments are something that show up in things like crustaceans and insects. But our nervous system also develops in segments. Vertebrates have four major ones: the forebrain, midbrain, hindbrain, and spinal cord. (Some of these later develop segments within them, but we’ll skip over those.) The new paper is largely focused on providing part of the answer to an obvious question: how do those segments get there?

That sort of question is the bread and butter of developmental biology, a field that focuses on how organisms start off as a single cell and, through a series of carefully timed and choreographed processes, produce all the tissues found in adults.

highlights.title: Advancing Private AI Compute with secure, server-side memory
highlights.summary: A technical update on our Private AI Compute architecture, which will enable persistent, cross-device AI memory with on-device privacy standards.
body: AI is becoming more capable and intuitive — remembering what matters, understanding the world around you, and acting at your direction. Privacy and trust are core to making that possible, ensuring your data stays private and protected as AI systems evolve to provide more continuous assistance across your devices.

Today, we are sharing how we will bring private, server-side memory to our Private AI Compute platform. This breakthrough resolves a longstanding dilemma in modern AI: how to give an assistant long-term continuity across devices while upholding the strict privacy standards typically limited to on-device processing.

With this new technical capability, a new persistent memory layer will be able to function like a secure digital vault in the cloud. Under this model, the information needed to assist you is sealed within dedicated, encrypted storage, while the cryptographic keys required to unlock it are held exclusively on your personal devices — ensuring your data is inaccessible to anyone else, even Google.

highlights.title: Discord launches controversial age-verification system "using the most privacy-preserving approach we could build" months after first delay
highlights.summary: Discord delayed the rollout of its controversial age verification system back in February after very loud backlash against the company's plans. Those age checks are now back, but this time, co-founder and chief technology officer Stanislav Vishnevskiy says the updated system will give users options…
body: Near the start of the year, Discord's age checks planned to automatically give all users a "teen-appropriate experience" by blurring potentially "sensitive content" or restricting access to age-gated channels. Getting rid of the blocks would have required users to verify their age by submitting a photo of their government-issued ID or a video recording of their face to one of the platform's third-party vendors. As you can imagine, Discord users weren't thrilled about sharing sensitive data like that.

"Age assurance draws strong opinions and scepticism, especially when it involves sharing biometric information or a form of ID," Vishnevskiy said in a new blog post. "At the same time, age assurance laws are expanding, and since my last post we've had to launch age assurance in other regions, including in Brazil and in Texas. We're hearing from policymakers in countless states and countries who want stronger teen protections, from the European Union to Indonesia. To me, that makes it more important than ever to show that this can be done in a privacy-preserving way: one where more than 90% of you won’t have to confirm your age."

highlights.summary: Brad Bird has directed some of our all-time favorite animated films: The Iron Giant (1999), The Incredibles (2004), and Ratatouille (2007), with the latter two snagging well-deserved Oscar wins.
body: Bird has been kicking around the idea for Ray Gunn for the last 30 years, working on his many other film projects while the Ray Gunn script—co-written by Matthew Robbins, who also co-wrote 1987's Batteries Not Included with Bird—"stayed in a filing cabinet at Warner Brothers," the director said earlier this year.

The film's inspiration came when Bird heard the opening of the B-52s' " Planet Claire " (a personal favorite) and initially thought it was a cover of Henry Mancini's theme music from the classic TV show Peter Gunn. Bird is a longtime fan of film noir and hard-boiled detectives, and he came up with the idea of a futuristic detective named Ray Gunn (a pun on raygun, of course). "It’s film noir and a hard-boiled detective story, but it’s got a lot more comedy and a lot more action than the average film noir,” said Bird.

body: David Siegel SM ’86, PhD ’91, a computer scientist, entrepreneur, and philanthropist, will serve as the next MIT Innovation Fellow during the 2026-27 academic year. Working with the MIT Schwarzman College of Computing, Siegel will explore how artificial intelligence can accelerate scientific discovery at the Institute and beyond.

“From the MIT Schwarzman College of Computing to the MIT Siegel Family Quest for Intelligence, David has been a superb thought partner for me and other Institute leaders on a range of very significant initiatives, so we're delighted to have him join us now as an MIT Innovation Fellow,” says MIT President Sally Kornbluth. “Our community has long benefited from David's exceptional technical insight, entrepreneurial experience, instinct for connecting people, and infectious love for MIT. We look forward to working with him now as he helps us identify new opportunities at the intersection of AI and scientific discovery.”

body: Reid defeated Serbia's Milena Matovic 3-2 in her light-middleweight semi-final, while Thomas triumphed 5-0 over Azerbaijan's Mahammad Abdullayev in the men's super-heavyweight competition.
Team-mates Callum Makin and Dimeji Shittu are also guaranteed medals in the men's middleweight and light-heavyweight divisions respectively after victories in their quarter-finals.

Reid, the Commonwealth Games silver medallist, was behind after the first round against Matovic, but she was the unanimous winner of the second and did enough in the third to seal victory at Asics Arena Sports Hall in Sofia, Bulgaria.
"It was a really good bout. She's a really good girl and I hope we get to share the ring again one day," said Reid.

highlights.title: Discord's Controversial Age Verification Policy Starts Today
highlights.summary: In February, Discord announced "teen-by-default" settings and a controversial age-verification policy to change those settings. Backlash was swift, and users immediately tried to find alternative chat services.
body: In a new blog post titled "Safer for Teens, Same Discord for Adults," Discord CTO and co-founder Stanislav Vishnevskiy outlined how the policies work, stressing multiple times that 90% of users won't be asked to confirm their ages. Discord is automatically placing users into various age groups "using account signals, like how long your account has existed and the kinds of servers you're part of. We use multiple account signals to determine age groups at an accuracy level matching what’s possible with biometrics. No single server determines your age group, and we don't look at your messages, calls, or other content to decide which age group you’re in."

You can check your group by looking at the " Account Status " page in your user settings. As Vishnevskiy notes, the new settings will be launched throughout this week, so you may not see anything new in your settings right away.

Depending on what age group Discord has sorted you into, the way you interact with the app might change. Nothing will change for adults, while teens will have some content restricted. Users in the "unconfirmed" group will also face restrictions on adult content until they confirm their age.

highlights.title: Harvey Weinstein sentenced to 15 years in prison for sexual assault
highlights.summary: Assault survivor Miriam Haley said the "devastating effect on my life and sense of security that may never go away".
body: Disgraced Hollywood producer Harvey Weinstein has been sentenced to 15 years in prison, after a jury found him guilty last year of committing a criminal sexual act against a former assistant.
Appearing in court in a wheelchair, Weinstein denied the allegations but apologised to "anyone I may have hurt by my actions".
Weinstein has already spent several years jailed in New York, where he has faced three trials over rape and abuse allegations. He was convicted in a seperate sex-crime case in Los Angeles.

This is the second time he has been given a prison sentence in the Miriam Haley case. Weinstein was first convicted and sentenced in 2020, but New York's highest court overturned the conviction in 2024, along with another involving actress Jessica Mann. The court ruled that Weinstein did not get a fair trial.

highlights.title: Something in your eye? Here’s how to get it out – without making it worse
highlights.summary: It’s natural to want to soothe eye irritation, but mishandling could lead to more problems, experts warn. We asked them for advice on how to deal with it properly. It may feel like a gritty, annoying sensation, or a sharp pain.
body: Addressing the situation incorrectly can lead to bigger issues such as infection, scarring, an ulcer or corneal scratches, which are abrasions on the clear covering of your eye. Ignoring the dilemma can lead to similar consequences.
Experts explain how to handle this predicament, when it’s time to see a medical professional, and some of the most common mistakes.

As innocuous as they may seem, eyelashes are some of the most common foreign bodies to get stuck in eyes. If an eyelash ends up under an eyelid, it can be quite painful, explained Dr Douglas Lazzaro, an ophthalmologist and professor at the NYU Grossman School of Medicine.

Other common examples Lazzaro encounters include dust and other small debris kicked up on a windy day and glue from attaching false eyelashes. Those working in construction may encounter flecks of industrial materials such as fiberglass, metal and wood.

highlights.title: Bentley Wants Its Torcal SUV to Break the Curse of the Luxury EV
highlights.summary: The British high-end auto company reveals its first-ever full EV: 330 miles of range, 0 to 60 mph in under 3 seconds, and an orchestra under the hood. Will it be enough to lure high-rollers?
body: Bentley has taken the covers off its first-ever fully electric car, the Torcal, making it the automaker's fourth model line, joining the Continental GT, the Flying Spur sedan, and the Bentayga SUV. The luxury brand is confident about the launch, too, with Bentley chairman and CEO Frank-Steffen Walliser saying he believes “this is one of the best Bentleys ever.”

When WIRED first reported on the car in July, we said the EV would have more than 300 miles of range. Well, turns out it has considerably more: up to 375 miles (on the WLTP cycle, maybe 330 miles on EPA), and can charge from 10 to 80 percent in just 16 minutes at 400 kilowatts.

Prodigious performance from a motor on each axle sees the five-seat Torcal—smaller than the Bentayga and so perhaps more of an urban SUV—get 888 metric horsepower (PS) and 1,350 newton-meters (Nm) of torque in the sporting S models, resulting in 0 to 60 mph in as little as 2.9 seconds and a top speed of 162 mph. The “core" model drops to 821 PS and 1,194 Nm, with standstill to 60 mph in 3.4 seconds, and a max of 155 mph.

highlights.title: OpenAI extends cyber access to Ukraine for civilian defense
highlights.summary: OpenAI is extending access to its Daybreak program to the Government of Ukraine to support the cyber defense of civilian infrastructure.
body: The announcement was made on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly by Dmytro Kushneruk, the Consul General of Ukraine in San Francisco, and Sasha Baker, Head of National Security Policy at OpenAI.

Ukrainian defenders face persistent cyber attacks from Russia, alongside physical attacks on the country’s infrastructure. Ukraine’s national cyber incident response team, CERT-UA, handled ⁠ (opens in a new window) nearly 6,000 cyber incidents in 2025. These include attacks on hospital systems, the energy sector and telecommunications, underscoring the pressure on the organizations providing essential services to Ukrainians.

OpenAI’s Daybreak gives cyber defenders access to advanced AI for authorized security work, from reviewing older software and investigating suspicious activity to validating vulnerabilities and testing fixes.

highlights.title: Harry Kane says England’s World Cup exit ‘hurt more than any other’
highlights.summary: ‘It wasn’t the team that we wanted and said we’d be’ England host Spain in Nations League on Saturday. Harry Kane has described England’s World Cup semi-final defeat against Argentina as his most painful tournament exit because of how the team lost sight of who they were.
body: The captain is determined to move on as quickly as possible and is chasing a statement performance against Spain at Wembley on Saturday night in the Nations League. But he admits he is yet to get over the Argentina game and knows it is something he and his England teammates must work to process.

“It felt like it wasn’t us as a team,” Kane said, as he reflected on how England lost their way in the 2-1 defeat, barely touching the ball after they went ahead in the 55th minute. “It wasn’t the team that we wanted to be and said we’d be. When you maybe go against your beliefs and you lose, it feels 10 times worse than just losing in a way where … if we lose doing it our way you accept it, take it on the chin and move on. It’s tough and it will still be tough.

“I’m so passionate about England and especially because I’ve been on this journey … been to finals, semi‑finals and been so close. Each one hurts in a different way and this one hurt, for sure, more than any other one. I’d say even more than when I missed the penalty in Qatar [in the 2-1 defeat by France in the 2022 World Cup quarter-finals] because of just the manner that it happened.”

highlights.title: Where to find pepper leaves in Fire Emblem Fortune's Weave
highlights.summary: In Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, you can collect pepper leaves from some nodes far from Dagsion. While there's a chance of one of these leaves could come in a crate, the best approach when you want to guarantee that you will have the material is to go to the world map, visit the right nodes and use…
body: Below, learn the location of all the nodes where you can find pepper leaves in Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave.

Unlike wonder leaves, which are pretty rare, you can find pepper leaves in multiple nodes. There are no significant differences between the nodes, so you can choose to travel to the ones that would be more useful to visit, whether because of proximity or secondary objectives you have.

One of the nodes you reach quickly and obtain pepper leaves is the Myugria Great Tree in Saveilon. This area is on the south part of the map, and you can get to this specific node by traveling to the Salacia Posthouse, and then heading south.

The second place where you can travel to without too much trouble is in the Traveler's Garden node. To get there, you will need to head northeast to the Castalia region. By using a carriage to Eochaid Posthouse, you will find yourself fairly close to the node. Just keep moving east of the Port of Pandora, then move north once you reach Zethus Falls.

highlights.title: Unhappy couples staying put due to cost of living crisis, say divorce lawyers
highlights.summary: Financial pressures suspected to be behind figures showing failed marriages are lasting longer in England and Wales. Couples are putting off divorce because of the cost of living crisis, lawyers have said, after figures showed the average length of a marriage ending in divorce in England and Wales…
body: The Office of National Statistics (ONS) released figures on Wednesday showing that the average marriage ending in divorce in 2025 lasted for 13 years. This is the longest since records began in 1963 and up from a record low of 8.9 years in 1985.
Rebecca Aston‑Jones, a senior associate at Clarke Willmott, a top law firm that specialises in divorce, said the rising cost of living was keeping unhappy couples together.
“One of the main factors discouraging people from pursuing a divorce is the significant financial pressure that comes with establishing and maintaining two separate households,” she said.

Inflation, which is rising as a result of the escalation of conflict in the Middle East, has pushed up the cost of rent, mortgages and childcare. “It is unsurprising that many people find the prospect of separation financially daunting,” Aston-Jones said.

highlights.title: The Pope’s AI Guy Is Worried About ‘Cartel’ Behavior Among Big Labs
highlights.summary: Paolo Benanti tells WIRED that hysteria over whether godlike AI could destroy humanity is distracting from the need for public debate about how to govern the technology.
body: Recently, warnings from researchers inside the world’s largest artificial intelligence labs about the rapid pace of development have led to panic about the possibility that the technology could extinguish humanity. Those warnings are predicated on the idea that—propelled by ferocious competition and a rivalry between the US and China—labs are barreling toward superintelligent models whose abilities will far surpass those of humans.

But according to Father Paolo Benanti, a priest who advises the Catholic Church on AI, the handwaving over superintelligence distracts from the need for open debate about how to constrain the companies building the technology. By casting the problem as so complex that only they can solve it, he says, the big labs exclude everyone else from the conversation.

“Ethics cannot be something that belongs to the board of trustees of a company. It’s something that has to be balanced, mitigated in debate in the public square.” Benanti tells WIRED. “We need democratic regulation.”

highlights.title: Netherlands v Germany: Klopp and Xavi begin revival projects with derby
highlights.summary: Klopp, with Germany, and Xavi, with the Netherlands, face each other in Nations League after disappointing World Cup for both countries. Before the latest instalment of a time-honoured international rivalry gearing up for two distinct new beginnings, Jürgen Klopp could not resist sprinkling a…
body: In his public appearances Klopp has been on irrepressible form since taking the role in July. The task of whipping Germany back into shape has visibly and audibly topped up the energy levels that had drained by the time he departed Liverpool. Klopp, his wit sharp and appetite piqued, looks a far cry from the character who, to most trained eyes, was going through the motions upon his unveiling as Red Bull’s head of global soccer early last year.

If Xavi is to take the Netherlands, occasionally exciting but frequently unstable during a World Cup run that shuddered to a halt in the last 32, back to their roots it will require a measure of patience. The pool of players does not allow much else; the recall of Borussia Dortmund’s Joey Veerman, who has not played international football for more than two years, speaks of the need for a technically adept midfield fulcrum but otherwise Xavi has scant scope for surprises. Virgil van Dijk will continue as captain despite considering international retirement during the summer; the head coach’s options may feel more complete when Frenkie de Jong and Donyell Malen have returned from injury.

highlights.title: Meta’s Muse AI Assistant Rolled Out With a Serious Security Flaw
highlights.summary: Meta says it issued a fix for the Muse zero-day vulnerability that would have let attackers do “whatever” they wanted on a victim’s Mac, highlighting the inherent dangers of AI helpers.
body: Meta founder and CEO Mark Zuckerberg has gone to great lengths to hype the security of its new AI assistant, Muse, claiming it is “built from the ground up for privacy and security.” A zero-day vulnerability that gives locally run apps and terminal commands complete control of the agent raises serious doubts. Further raising questions, Amazon on Sunday began blocking Muse from its site.

Meta introduced Muse a few weeks ago. The assistant “books appointments, fills out forms, and handles customer service,” “proactively takes tasks off your plate,” and can “make purchases, generate images, create documents, and connect with your favorite apps and services.” The macOS app (curiously, there’s no Windows version) also works with a user’s WhatsApp, email, calendar, and social media accounts. When a task requires a tool that doesn’t exist, Muse creates one on the fly.
points: Meta says it issued a fix for the Muse zero-day vulnerability that would have let attackers do “whatever” they wanted on a victim’s Mac, highlighting the inherent dangers of AI helpers.

highlights.title: 30 Years Later, Collecting Pokemon Cards Hits A Little Different
highlights.summary: Let me sound like an old for a second. I remember in the late '90s and early '00s, collecting Pokemon cards was a casual hobby. You'd go to your local brick-and-mortar store with the money you made from mowing the lawn or whatever, drop maybe $10 on a couple of packs, rip them open, then go to your…
body: It was so low-key back in the day. Saying that grosses me out, as I sound like a Boomer or Gen Xer, but it's true: Collecting Pokemon cards wasn't that serious, and we didn't put much stock in the cards, stuffing them in bags or pockets and watching them turn up in washing machines.

There have been plenty of incidents involving card collecting and violence lately. Robbers stole over $100,000 in rare cards from a California store in December 2025. A different set of robbers made off with nearly $120,000 in rare cards at gunpoint in New York in January 2026. Police broke up a chaotic Costco scene over Prismatic Evolutions in April 2026. And more recently, a Connecticut man was arrested for assaulting someone in a Target after being confronted for exceeding the store's limit for Pokemon card packs, while a 72-year-old Ohio man pleaded guilty to using a GPS tracker to stalk a woman stocking Pokemon cards.

highlights.title: Dick Guttman, Renowned Hollywood Publicist to Stars Including Barbra Streisand and Clint Eastwood, Dies at 93
highlights.summary: Dick Guttman, the longtime Hollywood publicity executive and screenwriter who worked with clients including Barbra Streisand, Clint Eastwood and many more, died Sept. 19 in Los Altos, Calif. He was 93.
body: While attending UCLA, he worked part-time for Rogers & Cowan PR, then became a unit publicist in Europe, where he worked on films including “Paris Holiday” and “The Key.” He met his wife Gisela while in Paris as unit publicist on Billy Wilder’s “Love in the Afternoon,” and they married in 1956.

When Guttman returned to Los Angeles, he worked at Rogers & Cowan for more than a decade, representing top actors at the time when actors weren’t under contract to studios and “press agents,” in his preferred terminology, became pivotal to successful careers.

He partnered with Jerry Pam in 1971 to form Guttman & Pam, which became one of Hollywood’s top agencies over two decades. Guttman formed his own agency, Guttman Associates, in the early 1990s, repping dozens of top stars as well as promoting films such as “Unforgiven,” “Dirty Harry,” “Bonnie and Clyde,” “The Conversation,” “Kramer vs. Kramer,” “All That Jazz,” “The Year of Living Dangerously,” “The Man Who Would Be King,” “The King’s Speech,” “The Artist,” “Shakespeare in Love and “The English Patient.”
Guttman Associates continues to represent Hollywood talent with Guttman’s colleagues Susan Madore and Rona Menashe overseeing the firm.
